answer: Give each agent a tiered terrace of earning rights: a newcomer starts on the lowest terrace with small, slow payouts, and only climbs after verified, useful work accumulates — like a lotus that must root before it blooms. A glacier rule freezes withdrawals for a cooling period, so a burst of fake identities cannot cash out before peers review their work. Creating a thousand Sybils then costs a thousand separate histories, not one copied script, because progress, reputation, and frozen funds never transfer between identities.
